Check: Freeze product edits, then export from the Products panel.
Details: Why it bites: open the Products & Services panel, click Products, then Export all, or tick the checkbox beside the featured image and click Export. "You can export up to 10,000 products." Later edits do not flow back into that file.

Check: Treat the file as physical and service products, and leave download products off the import.
Details: Why it bites: the Export all steps are headed Export all physical and service products, and the selection steps carry no such heading. The download-products page says it is not possible "to export download products." The import page lists download products as not importable.

Check: Check gift cards in your own export.
Details: Why it bites: the export article and the import article do not mention them. The inventory page says you can bulk edit "physical and service products" from a products .csv, and it does not mention gift cards. Whether a gift card row is exported is not said.

Check: Read the subscription sentence as a move between Squarespace sites.
Details: Why it bites: the import limitations say "You can’t move customer subscriptions between Squarespace sites." The export article does not mention subscription products. Check in your own export before you treat one as missing or present.

Check: Count columns against the example, then look in your own export for columns the example does not have.
Details: Why it bites: the export page says the export "uses the same format as our import .csv" with an additional column for pages, and it does not name that column. The example has 26 columns, from `Product ID [Non Editable]` through `Hosted Image URLs`, and it includes `Product Page`, so check whether `Product Page` is that column. It has no `GTIN` and no `MPN`, which only the two move-between-sites tables on the import page list.

Check: Read a variant product as a first product row, then option rows, and keep the first row as a variant.
Details: Why it bites: for the sample with variants, "Row 3 is the First product row, and rows 4-8 are the Option rows." That first row holds the first option combination, the title, the product URL, categories, tags, visibility, and the images. Option rows repeat the option names and fill SKU, price, and stock.

Check: Check whether `Product ID [Non Editable]` repeats on option rows.
Details: Why it bites: the move steps say to make the cells beneath Product ID and Variant ID blank, while bulk edit says "Don't edit existing values," so an export can contain them. The Troubleshooting entry for a missing column says cell 2A contains a product ID, which disagrees with the move steps, and no page says the id repeats on an option row. The example leaves both id columns blank, and the import-from-another-platform tables say to leave them blank, so check in your own export.

Check: Map `Option Name 1` through `Option Value 3` only.
Details: Why it bites: the import tables document three Option Name and Option Value pairs, and each pair creates a variant, while the variants page allows six options in the .csv importer too. Squarespace does not say how options 4, 5, and 6 are written in an export, so check in your own export. "You can create up to 2,048 variants for a product," that page caps a product at three options, and some themes and apps might not support more than 100.

Check: When On Sale is Yes, put Sale Price in Shopify Price and Price in Compare-at price, and when On Sale is No or blank, keep Price and leave Compare-at price empty.
Details: Why it bites: "Only enter a sale price if the sale status is set as Yes (next column)." The example still fills Sale Price on No rows, which is the note above. Shopify's guide moves the two prices only on a Yes row and does not say what Compare-at price holds on other rows, so leaving it empty is this list's choice.

Check: Keep Compare-at price higher than Price on a row that should show a sale.
Details: Why it bites: Compare-at price must be higher than Price "to display the sale price." Only the sale price is displayed at checkout, and the theme controls whether and where a sale shows.

Check: Map a numeric Stock to Inventory tracker `shopify` and that quantity, and map `Unlimited` to a blank tracker and a blank quantity.
Details: Why it bites: Shopify's guide says to remove non-numerical characters from Stock and does not mention Unlimited, so removing the word leaves an empty cell. "The default value is 0 if no value is entered," so that empty cell is not unlimited while tracking stays on. A blank tracker means inventory isn't tracked, the Squarespace file has no backorder column, and the spelling note is above.

Check: Keep Weight, Length, Width, and Height as numbers until you know the store's unit, and do not invent a currency column.
Details: Why it bites: those four columns are in the example and the import tables, and "After the import, dimensions will match your store’s measurement standard." Neither the example nor the import tables have a unit column or a currency column, and prices display in the store's currency after import, so check in your own export. The orders file has a Currency column, which is a different export.

Check: Enter Shopify weight as whole grams after you know the unit, or leave the grams cell blank.
Details: Why it bites: the grams cell wants "only the numerical value, without the unit of measurement or decimals," so 5.125 kilograms is `5125`, and a blank cell becomes 0. The guide's pounds factor gives 1814.4 for 4 pounds, so drop the decimals, as the grams note above says. Leave Length, Width, and Height out of the packed-product columns.

Check: Set Status and Published on online store from Visible, on purpose.
Details: Why it bites: Visible is Yes or No, on the first product row only, and an import can only publish or hide ("You can’t schedule products with an import"). What a scheduled product shows in Visible is not said, so check your own export. Shopify's guide maps Yes and No to true and false on Published on online store, and a missing Status column uploads the product as active, so set Status to `active`, `draft`, or `archived`.

Check: Put one category label in Type, copy Tags, and leave Collection empty.
Details: Why it bites: Shopify's guide says "Squarespace exports categories as URL paths, such as /clothing/blouses," and to replace each path with one product type. The example and the import tables disagree, which is the categories note, and tags stay comma-separated on the first product row, up to 80 characters per tag. Collection is import-only, one collection, 255 characters, and absent from a Shopify export.

Check: Copy Product URL into the URL handle, then copy that handle onto every variant row and image row.
Details: Why it bites: the cell is the slug without a leading slash, 3 to 200 characters, dashes, first product row only, and capitals become lowercase. "In version 7.1, product URLs always include a p/ before the customizable URL slug" so the live path is the store page, that prefix, and the cell. Shopify's guide allows letters, dashes, and numbers, and bars spaces, accents, and periods.

Check: Split the image cell into one Product image URL per row, and leave alt text and variant images empty.
Details: Why it bites: the export omits Featured Images, Product image alt text, and Variant images. "Separate multiple images with spaces or line breaks," on the first product row only, and the upload file cannot assign variant images. Shopify takes one URL per row, downloads the file during import, says the file name should not include `_thumb`, `_small`, or `_medium` suffixes, and allows 512 characters of alt text, which this export does not contain.

Check: Leave customers, orders, reviews, redirects, the pages column, and options 4 through 6 out of the Shopify product CSV.
Details: Why it bites: the column table has no column for those, and a product can have up to 3 options. It does have `Weight unit for display` and `Packed product dimension unit`, which the Squarespace example has no column for, and its price columns take the amount without a currency symbol. "you can't create a gift card by importing a product CSV file," and SEO title allows 70 characters and SEO description 320.

Check: Export the customer list you actually opened, and keep it apart from the product file.
Details: Why it bites: the Lists & Segments file lists Account, names, Email, order totals, last-order date, Customer Since, last-used addresses, Tags, and no password, and "Notes aren't included in the exported .csv file." Shopify's guide uses Contacts and Export all contacts, omits notes and saved addresses except the latest physical order's address, and names the Squarespace columns Accepts Marketing and Shipping Address 1, which are not in Squarespace's export column list, so check the headings in your download.

Check: Import customers only after the file uses Shopify's customer headings.
Details: Why it bites: "You can't import a customer CSV that doesn't match the Shopify headings," and the same caution says there is no data mapping support for customer CSV imports. The guide's province column wants the province or state ISO code, and it says the country column is not in the Squarespace download. Shopify's customer import page limits a file to 15 MB, does not migrate passwords, and does not import the Total Spent and Total Orders columns.

Check: Export orders from Products & Services, then Orders, then Export data, then Download CSV, and move history with an app, not the product CSV.
Details: Why it bites: "You can export orders for active, visible products only," chosen by status and by the date the order was created. A partial refund still shows the full line price, and hidden products, products on disabled store pages, and earlier versions of renamed products are left out. Shopify's guide treats historical orders as fulfilled and sends them through an app such as EZ Importer.

Check: Copy pages and posts across by hand.
Details: Why it bites: Squarespace's site-content export is an .xml file in WordPress format, and "Only one blog page exports." Store pages and product blocks are in its list of content that doesn't export, and Shopify's guide repeats the WordPress .xml and one-blog-page limits and adds that you can't import the file into Shopify. The hub page lists site content, products, and contacts as three separate exports.

Check: Plan reviews on their own.
Details: Why it bites: the product export will not include customer reviews, and Shopify's guide says "Customer reviews can't be exported." The product CSV has no reviews column.

Check: Save the Squarespace URL mappings you still need, then build those redirects again on Shopify.
Details: Why it bites: mappings live under Developer tools as `/old-url -> /new-url 301`, and the URL mappings field "has a limit of 400 KB, which is usually around 2500 redirect lines." A 301 needs the old URL gone and the new URL present, and a redirect works only after the old page is deleted or disabled. A 7.1 example is `/store/p/[name] -> /buy/p/[name] 301`, and the page says you can only redirect from domains connected to your Squarespace site.

Check: Add a Shopify URL redirect for every old path you still need, and read the live path before you write it.
Details: Why it bites: the product CSV has no redirect column. The handle "is used in the URL of the product page," and on 7.1 the old path also has the store page and `p/` before the slug. Shopify's redirects page says redirects work only from broken URLs and lists prefixes it cannot redirect, including `/shop`, so check a Squarespace store page slug against that list.

Check: Spot-check one variant product, one On Sale No row whose Sale Price is filled, one `Unlimited` stock cell, and one Visible value.
Details: Why it bites: Shopify's guide says imported products marked as hidden "aren't published until you make them available to your sales channels," and that a product missing a variant option won't be imported successfully. On [test-catalogs/squarespace-basic](test-catalogs/squarespace-basic), `JAR-S` is on sale, `JAR-L` and `LADLE-FERN` keep the regular price, and `CLOTH-MIST` is the unlimited row.

Check: Place test orders before you call checkout done.
Details: Why it bites: Shopify's Migrate from Squarespace guide lists a successful and a failed transaction, refunding and canceling an order, fulfilling or partially fulfilling an order, and archiving a successful order as test orders to run. It says to try them "to make sure that everything is working".

Check: Recount rows against the frozen export.
Details: Why it bites: the import article's sample calls row 2 "a single product with no variants", and rows 3-8 are one product, and its first row is an option combination. A SKU can be blank, because Squarespace generates it, and Shopify's CSV guide puts all of a simple product's fields on its first row and uses later rows only for extra images. On `test-catalogs/squarespace-basic`, the rows are `JAR-S`, `JAR-L`, `LADLE-FERN`, and `CLOTH-MIST`, and Shopify's guide says a product missing a variant option won't be imported successfully.

Check: Request the old URLs that used to get the most visits.
Details: Why it bites: Squarespace says redirects work only from the old page once it is deleted or disabled, and only from domains connected to your Squarespace site, so do not assume a mapping answers on a Shopify store. Read each new path from the live page.
